_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2014 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2014 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +75% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.10; conservative 2yr -13%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY05-FY14, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-8.1%/yr (FY15 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +5.2%/yr (FY05-FY14 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +84.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY05-FY14); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2015-04-17) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (90.4% downside to Bear $8 / +-3.9% upside to Bull $80) | Adj composite 1.80 vs market 2.90: gap -1.10 [OVERVALUED] | +75% above the EPP floor $48 (10x FY15E $4.75) | Conservative 2-yr case: -13.2% total (-6.6%/yr) | At 17.5x FY15E the 15% hurdle price $110 sits above the BULL case; Machinery sales -9.5% in Q4 2014, forward revenues -9.4% (FY15 sales and revenues guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Caterpillar FY2014 10-K and Exhibit 13

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: fourth-quarter 2014 results release
sources.supports: fourth-quarter 2014 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results, full-year 2014 actuals and 2013 profit per share excluding restructuring costs; 2015 outlook: sales and revenues about $50 billion, profit $4.75 per share excluding restructuring costs ($4.60 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: third-quarter 2014 results release
sources.supports: third-quarter 2014 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2014 outlook: sales and revenues about $55 billion, profit $6.50 per share excluding restructuring costs ($6.00 including them); preliminary 2015 sales and revenues flat to slightly up
